Hi Alex — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the items we discussed that will unblock procurement: 

1) Payment preference: you mentioned AP typically issues POs for new vendors over $25k but will use a corporate card for pilots under $5k. Can you confirm the threshold and whether P-card (corporate credit card) is acceptable for pilot billing?

2) Vendor onboarding items AP needs: W-9 (or equivalent), vendor form (Coupa vendor registration), invoice remit details, and a signed MSA/SOW for production. I attached our vendor onboarding packet and a sample PO template for your procurement team to review.

3) Commercial path options we can support:
- Direct invoicing to SC Systems (Net 30 available on approval)
- P-card for pilot (instant)
- AWS Marketplace (metered SaaS) — helps centralize procurement but takes longer to onboard on the marketplace side

Grace — thanks for the write-up. A few clarifications from AP: 

- Threshold: our policy is to use PO for any vendor engagements anticipated above $20k annually. Under $5k we typically run on a P-card for pilots; between $5k–20k is case-by-case.
- Required docs: completed vendor registration in Coupa, W-9 (US vendors), standard insurance certificate, and signed commercial terms (MSA).
- Invoice terms: we prefer Net30, but some legal approvals needed for exceptions.

Quick questions for Redwood:
1) Can you accept a P-card for the pilot and then transition to a PO for production?
2) If we go marketplace (AWS), is Redwood able to provide a marketplace invoice to match our internal spend tracking?

Cc'ing Michael (ops) to connect on Coupa vendor onboarding. I'll introduce the AP contact once I confirm schedules.

Thanks,

Alex — appreciate the detail. Short answers and how we typically handle this for enterprise customers: 

1) P-card for pilot: yes, we can accept card for pilots under $5k. It's our fastest path to get you started. We frequently put a short-term pilot SOW on a card while formal PO and MSA weave through procurement.

2) Transition to PO for production: absolutely — once you have budget and approvals, AP can issue a PO and we will invoice against that PO. We can accommodate Net30 post-credit approval.

3) Marketplace (AWS): Redwood is listed on AWS Marketplace (metered SaaS). Marketplace billing will flow through AWS and can simplify internal chargeback for some customers, but it adds onboarding time (marketplace listing sync, entitlements). If you need centralized spend visibility in Coupa, we can provide the marketplace SKUs, but we usually recommend direct invoicing for faster PO issuance.

Required items to get a vendor record created in Coupa:
- Completed redwood_vendor_onboarding_packet.pdf (we can pre-fill most fields)
- Signed MSA (link to DocuSign below) or a PO referencing the MSA
- W-9 (attached in the packet)

Proposed next steps: 
- Grace to send the pre-filled onboarding packet to Procurement (we can share a redwood_vendor_packet_filled.pdf once you confirm contact)
- If you'd like the pilot this month, we can process the pilot SOW by card — I'll prepare a short DocuSign SOW (attached pilot_statement_of_work.docx draft) that Grace can push to you today.
- If procurement prefers PO-first, please share the target PO date so we can align technical onboarding and capacity.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/8421 (for reference)
DocuSign SOW link (placeholder): https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/signed-sow/abc123

Attachments: redwood_msa_docusign_link.txt (DocuSign contract), pilot_statement_of_work.docx

Happy to jump on a quick call with AP if that helps move Coupa onboarding faster.

Best,
